newsitem.title: UK: Swiss doctor tests new oral vaccine for infections.
newsitem.headline: Swiss doctor tests new oral vaccine for infections.

text.p: Swiss researchers said on Thursday they were testing a new "natural" vaccine that could protect people from some forms of food poisoning and dysentery.
They said they had figured out a way to grow proteins that make up part of the body's immune system.
Blaise Corthesy of the Swiss Institute for Experimental Cancer Research said the proteins could be taken orally to protect against a variety of infections.

He told a joint meeting of the British Society for Immunology and the Biochemical Society that his work centred on immunoglobulin A, which cells secrete naturally to fight invaders. It attaches itself to foreign bacteria, preventing them from attacking cells.
Corthesy said his group had grown cell lines -- batches of cells in a test tube -- that produced the two components of immunoglobulin A. When the two halves were joined, they made the protein.
This could be delivered orally because it occurs naturally in the stomach and intestine, so it would not be broken down by the digestive system.
Corthesy said it might be useful against intestinal infections like salmonella, which causes food poisoning, and shigella, which causes dysentery.
